body.heading: Chapter 1: The poster on the noticeboard
paragraphs: Sam saw the poster on the school noticeboard on Monday morning, and his heart did a little jump. THE GREAT KITE RACE, it said, in enormous gold letters. SATURDAY. THE BIG MEADOW. EVERYONE WELCOME. Sam had never flown a kite in a race before. He had never even flown a kite that stayed up for more than ten seconds. But by lunchtime, he had already decided: he was going to build one himself.

After school, Sam spread his materials on the kitchen table: two thin sticks, a sheet of red paper, string, glue, and ribbons for the tail. He worked all evening, tongue sticking out in concentration, until — ta-da! — a kite. It looked, Sam thought, extremely fast.

body.heading: Stop and think
paragraphs: Before you read on, think: Sam has never built a kite before, and the race is on Saturday. What do you think will happen when he tests his kite for the first time? Make a guess — then read on.

body.heading: The first flight
paragraphs: On Tuesday, Sam ran to the meadow with his kite and his little sister Lily. 'Ready?' he shouted. He ran as fast as he could, the kite bouncing behind him — up it went, up, up… and then it dived, spun round twice, and crashed straight into the branches of the old oak tree. Lily covered her mouth. Sam stared up at his beautiful kite, stuck high above their heads, its ribbons waving sadly in the breeze.

'Well,' said Sam at last, 'I have four days to fix it — and to learn how kites really fly.' He did not know it yet, but help was already on its way, from the most surprising person in the whole village. Who could it be? Find out in Chapter 2.

body.heading: Words to know
paragraphs: Meadow — a field of grass and wild flowers.
Dive — to rush downward quickly, head first.
Concentration — thinking very hard about one thing and nothing else.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Why do you think Sam's kite dived into the tree instead of flying? What might he need to change?
2. Who do you think the 'most surprising person' might be — and what makes you think so?

takeaway: Sam has entered the Great Kite Race, but his first kite is stuck in a tree. He has four days, one big problem, and a surprising helper on the way — in Chapter 2.
